parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of trans identity or same-sex conduct and visible trans participation lower catastrophic risk, but combined regime has no national anti-discrimination or recognition law, only patchwork provincial/city coverage, documented service refusals, trans killings in 2025 and earlier, and birth-sex male detention with reported abuse. If outed/arrested, custody and weak national recourse are severe; if not detained, everyday exposure is mainly discrimination and violence risk. This places it below working-protection anchors and above organised targeting.

entry_documents.exposure: No visitor border or marker-recognition rule documented; residents cannot correct birth-certificate sex, but home passport use by visitor is not documented as rejected.
entry_documents.protection: No criminalisation of trans identity; no documented entry denial for trans visitors.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch could arise only if authorities demand local records; no such visitor practice documented.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Trans women held in male facilities; capital jail ordinary male dorms, mandatory head-shaving, safety via inmate hierarchies and survival 'weddings' with male inmates.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: One southern jail annex batches LGBT detainees 'to prevent abuse'; no national placement rule documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest for scandal, assembly or other minor offences could lead to birth-sex custody, turning low-probability detention into severe harm.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No bathroom/facility law documented. Two local ordinances restrict gender expression/cross-dressing, one under imprisonment for a religious community, enforcement not documented.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Nine provinces and 32 cities/municipalities prohibit SOGI discrimination, coverage varying by locality.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Visitor protection depends on province/city; national patchwork leaves gaps and contrary local ordinances.

care_services.exposure: No visitor HRT import, prescription or emergency-care rule documented. Right-to-care card is for registered resident couples via power of attorney.
care_services.protection: HIV anti-discrimination statute and social-worker harassment penalties exist nationally, but visitor care continuity not documented.
care_services.interaction: Not documented. whether clinic care would out visitor or be refused.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No trans-specific criminal offence. Grave-scandal provision can punish highly scandalous public conduct; police arrested at least 20 Pride participants in 2020 under assembly/disease-reporting laws.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Women's/safe-spaces statutes punish transphobic slurs/ridicule; social-worker statute penalises SOGIE harassment.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Enforcement is for conduct/assembly, not identity per se, but provides a police lever if outed in a protest or public-affection context.

minors_guardians.exposure: No age-dependent visitor, school-enrolment or guardian rule documented. Resident-only school uniform and proposed LGR-for-minors policies do not govern visitors.
minors_guardians.interaction: Not documented. any distinct minor-specific exposure beyond adult regime.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Two trans women killed 23 June 2025, murders reported since 2012 including by armed groups, harassment in displacement camps, foreigner arrested for raping trans woman May 2025, drag performer struck 2024. No per-capita rate published.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Mayor apologised after 2024 stage attack; national human-rights commission investigates but lacks enforcement power without national law.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Violence is documented but rate, pattern frequency and state response outcomes are insufficient to establish a campaign; police also arrested Pride participants.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No national SOGI anti-discrimination law; equality bill stalled/rejected 2017-2022; establishments may refuse/refuse service and exclude gender-diverse people with little legal consequence nationally.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Patchwork provincial/city ordinances and specific harassment statutes provide local recourse; 2026 travel score for trans travellers 62 'Exercise Caution' method unpublished.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedy strength varies sharply by locality and is unavailable as a uniform national guarantee for a short-stay visitor.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: partial denial and uneven remedies without credible execution/detention pathway. This case has stronger patchwork protections but worse documented male-dorm custody and lethal violence, so at or slightly below 0.55.

Lower than 0.65-A: there national equality law, reliable release and compensation worked. Here no national equality law, commission lacks enforcement, and detention placement is by birth sex with reported abuse.

Higher than 0.25-C: no criminalisation of cross-dressing nationally, no routine raids or frequent custody, and some local protections and public acceptance. Custody practice alone is comparable, but probability of reaching custody is far lower.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: no identity criminalisation, border/facility bans or organised targeting, and local protections plus visible acceptance support reduced risk in covered cities. Against that, national recourse is absent, service refusal is documented, 2025 killings show lethal street risk without a derivable rate, and any detention leads to birth-sex male housing with documented abuse and only one annex mitigation. Custody severity and patchwork remedies keep the score in Elevated Risk despite low criminalisation.
